diagnosis: The issuer guard compares normalised names; _norm_name() strips non-alphanumerics, so spacing is irrelevant to matching.

The failure came from company_name being None: the frozen parser's broad name fallback cannot isolate a legal name from a heading line with no word separators, and _primary_issuer_header requires an identity block (CIN/registered office/'to be listed on') that this synthetic notice omits.

Same code, same pinned OCR packages, same font and same input file produced correctly separated text locally, so the difference is the OCR engine's segmentation on the runner, not a code or data difference.
The mode is fail-closed: ambiguous OCR rejects the document; it never accepts an unverified issuer.
not_done: No test, engine, config or fixture file was changed to make the run green.
open_decision: Option A: make the synthetic fixture realistic by adding a CIN/registered-office block so the intended _primary_issuer_header path is exercised; test-only change, leaves the broad-fallback fragility untested.
Option B: add space-tolerant heading normalisation in the OCR pre-pass outside the frozen parser; touches a verification-adjacent path and needs review, and must not repair digits or weights.
